papers.title: On the Relationship between Online Gaussian Process Regression and Kernel Least Mean Squares Algorithms
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between online Gaussian process (GP) regression and kernel least mean squares (KLMS) algorithms. While the latter have no capacity of storing the entire posterior distribution during online learning, we discover that their operation corresponds to the assumption of a fixed posterior covariance that follows a simple parametric model. Interestingly, several well-known KLMS algorithms correspond to specific cases of this model. The probabilistic perspective allows us to understand how each of them handles uncertainty, which could explain some of their performance differences.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文为在线高斯过程与核最小均方算法的理论比较，未涉及有限元分析或生物医学应用。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address expensive simulation sampling, constraint handling, uncertainty quantification for physical models, or transferability to implant/biomechanics design.

summary_zh.motivation: 揭示在线高斯过程回归与核最小均方算法之间的关系。
summary_zh.method: 理论推导了KLMS算法对应固定后验协方差的参数模型。
summary_zh.result: 发现多种KLMS算法是该模型的特例，解释了其不确定性处理差异。
summary_zh.validation: 无实验验证，纯理论分析。

summary_en.motivation: To theoretically clarify the relationship between online Gaussian process regression and kernel least mean squares algorithms.
summary_en.method: A parametric model for fixed posterior covariance is derived, showing that several KLMS algorithms are special cases.
summary_en.result: The probabilistic perspective explains performance differences among KLMS algorithms in terms of uncertainty handling.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; purely theoretical derivation.

papers.title: Tibial Revision Knee Arthroplasty: Influence of Modular Stems on Implant Fixation and Bone Flexibility in AORI Type T2a Defects
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Due to the varying bone defects presented to surgeons during revision total knee arthroplasty, modular implant systems are preferred over standard implant designs. However, every implant combination (sleeves, stems and augments) can affect the fixation in different ways and thus influence the long-term outcome. We therefore aimed to analyze the effect of large metaphyseal sleeves with and without short modular stems on implant fixation and bone flexibility of a modular tibial revision knee system. METHODS: A new tibial revision implant (Attune RP Revision; DePuy Synthes) with a sleeve was compared to a sleeve/stem combination implanted in synthetic bones with Anderson Orthopaedic Research Institute (AORI) Type T2a defects and also compared to an intact bone. Implant-bone-interface micromotions and bone deformations during standardized load application were measured using a digital image correlation system. RESULTS: The lowest relative micromotions were measured more distally for stemmed implants, and more proximally for the stemless group. When compared to an intact bone, there is increased proximal bone deformation in the stemless group. CONCLUSIONS: Using a short stem in addition to a tibial revision implant with a metaphyseal sleeve in a moderate bone defect provides for more natural bone deformation. Although the main fixation area was shifted distally, relative micromotions were reduced. Based on this biomechanical study, the use of diaphyseal short stems with metaphyseal sleeves seems to be beneficial in terms of the initial implant fixation and for its flexibility, which is similar to that of intact bones in the case of AORI T2a defects.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究膝关节翻修假体而非髋关节股骨柄，但涉及模块化柄对固定和骨变形的影响，与股骨柄应力遮挡和微动研究有间接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on tibial revision knee arthroplasty, not hip implant or femoral stem, and does not quantify stress shielding in Gruen zones or compare intact vs implanted femur.

summary_zh.motivation: 分析膝关节翻修术中模块化柄对假体固定和骨柔性的影响
summary_zh.method: 在AORI T2a缺损合成骨上植入带套筒和短柄的胫骨翻修假体，用数字图像相关测量微动和变形
summary_zh.result: 带短柄的假体远端微动更低，近端骨变形更接近完整骨
summary_zh.validation: 合成骨力学测试与数字图像相关测量

summary_en.motivation: To analyze the effect of modular stems on implant fixation and bone flexibility in tibial revision knee arthroplasty with moderate bone defects.
summary_en.method: Implanted tibial revision components with metaphyseal sleeves and short stems into synthetic bones with AORI Type T2a defects and measured micromotions and bone deformations using digital image correlation.
summary_en.result: Stemmed implants shifted the main fixation area distally with lower micromotions, while stemless implants increased proximal bone deformation.
summary_en.validation: Biomechanical testing on synthetic bones with digital image correlation.

papers.title: Histological Changes of the Acetabular Labrum in Coxarthrosis: Labral Degeneration and Repair
papers.abstract: Introduction The current study was designed to describe types of histological changes within the acetabular labrum in the advanced stages of coxarthrosis, in patients requiring total hip arthroplasty (THA). Methods 77 consecutive patients without systemic disorders or prior hip surgery, scheduled for THA with 3 types of coxarthrosis: avascular necrosis (AVN), idiopathic, and dysplastic coxarthrosis were analysed. Patient's data: age, gender, side of the involvement, duration of the symptoms were recorded, and standard anteroposterior (AP) radiographic views of the pelvis were obtained. During THA procedure the acetabular labrum was harvested and examined histologically and immunohistochemically. The mean chondrocytes number and density were calculated using morphometric techniques. Results In 77 analysed acetabular labra the following histological changes were found: heterogenic matrix, foci of granular matrix breakdown, pseudocysts, intralabral c alcifications, chondrocyte apoptosis, inflammatory reaction with lymphocytes infiltration and macrophages infiltration and vascular proliferation with 2 stages of maturation: endothelial cell formation and fully formed blood vessels. The average chondrocytes density was 478 cells in 1 mm 2 and significantly decreased with age. Conclusions The acetabular labrum is an important part of the process of degeneration of the hip in osteoarthritis (OA). Vascular formation and cellular infiltration found in the damaged fibrocartilage may represent a labral response to degenerative changes.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究髋臼盂唇的组织学变化，与股骨柄假体的应力遮挡、微动或骨-植入物界面力学无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on histological changes of the acetabular labrum in osteoarthritis, with no quantification of femoral stem stress shielding, micromotion, contact mechanics, or bone-implant interface mechanics.

summary_zh.motivation: 描述晚期髋关节病中髋臼盂唇的组织学变化类型。
summary_zh.method: 对77例THA患者的盂唇进行组织学和免疫组化分析。
summary_zh.result: 发现基质降解、假性囊肿、钙化、炎症及血管增生，软骨细胞密度随年龄下降。
summary_zh.validation: 无力学验证，仅组织学观察。

summary_en.motivation: To characterize histological changes in the acetabular labrum during advanced coxarthrosis in patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: Histological and immunohistochemical analysis of acetabular labra harvested from 77 THA patients with different coxarthrosis types.
summary_en.result: Degenerative changes including matrix breakdown, pseudocysts, calcifications, inflammation, and vascular proliferation were observed; chondrocyte density decreased significantly with age.
summary_en.validation: No mechanical validation; purely histological and immunohistochemical assessment.
